verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Hand-checked: one fission of ²³⁵U releases on average about 2.5 neutrons (the book rounds this to "nearly three"), and each of these can cause a further fission, so the reaction sustains itself. The book gives the definition alone; the mechanism is added here because the word "self-sustained" needs it.

steps.margin_note: First mark. The neutrons from one fission start the next fissions.
steps.why: Fission produces the very particle that triggers fission, so the process is self-sustained — that is the whole idea behind the word "chain".
common_mistakes: Saying the energy causes the next fission. It is the neutrons.
Naming no fuel. The mark scheme expects ²³⁵U or uranium.

recall.must_convey: That one fission of uranium-235 releases about three neutrons, which cause fission in further nuclei.
accept: uranium two thirty five splits and gives neutrons

steps.memory_tip: Fission needs a neutron and makes about three — that is why the reaction is self-sustained.

steps.label: The definition
steps.mark_note: Self-sustained fission reaction releasing large energy

this kind, releasing a large amount of energy,

lines.text: Chain reaction: fission that sustains itself

steps.margin_note: Second mark. The phrase "self-sustained fission reaction" is the one the examiner looks for.
steps.why: The definition names three things at once: the reaction is fission, it sustains itself through its own neutrons, and it releases a large amount of energy.
common_mistakes: Calling it a fusion reaction. A chain reaction is a fission process.
Leaving out "self-sustained". That word is the definition.

recall.must_convey: That a chain reaction is a self-sustained nuclear fission reaction that releases a large amount of energy.
accept: releases a large amount of energy
the reaction continues on its own

steps.memory_tip: Self-sustained is the key word: no outside supply of neutrons is needed.

insider_note: Two marks: one for the neutrons that carry the reaction forward, one for the phrase "self-sustained fission reaction".
